task.title: Restoring Red Hat Quay on standalone deployments
task.shortdesc: To restore a standalone Red Hat Quay deployment from backup, you can restore configuration files, recreate the PostgreSQL database, and sync blobs to object storage.

ul.li: You have backed up your Red Hat Quay deployment.

step.cmd: Create a new directory that bind-mounts to /conf/stack inside of the Red Hat Quay container:
Copy the contents of your temporary backup directory created in the backup procedure to the new-quay-install directory created in Step 1:
Change into the new-quay-install directory by entering the following command:
Extract the contents of your Red Hat Quay directory:

info.codeblock: config.yaml config.yaml.bak extra_ca_certs/ extra_ca_certs/ca.crt ssl.cert ssl.key

step.cmd: Recall the DB_URI from your backed-up config.yaml file by entering the following command:
Run the following command to enter the PostgreSQL database server:
Enter psql and create a new database in 172.24.10.50 to restore the quay databases, for example, example_restore_registry_quay_database, by entering the following command:

info.codeblock: $ psql "host=172.24.10.50 port=5432 dbname=postgres user=<username> password=test123" postgres=> CREATE DATABASE example_restore_registry_quay_database;

step.cmd: Connect to the database by running the following command:

info.codeblock: You are now connected to database "example-restore-registry-quay-database" as user "postgres".

step.cmd: Create a pg_trgm extension of your Quay database by running the following command:

info.codeblock: example_restore_registry_quay_database=> CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm;

step.cmd: Exit the postgres CLI by entering the following command:
Import the database backup to your new database by running the following command:

info.p: Update the value of DB_URI in your config.yaml from postgresql://<username>:test123@172.24.10.50/quay to postgresql://<username>:test123@172.24.10.50/example-restore-registry-quay-database before restarting the Red Hat Quay deployment.

note.p: The DB_URI format is DB_URI postgresql://<login_user_name>:<login_user_password>@<postgresql_host>/<quay_database>. If you are moving from one PostgreSQL server to another PostgreSQL server, update the value of <login_user_name>, <login_user_password> and <postgresql_host> at the same time.

step.cmd: In the /opt/new-quay-install directory, print the contents of your DISTRIBUTED_STORAGE_CONFIG bundle:

info.codeblock: DISTRIBUTED_STORAGE_CONFIG: default: DISTRIBUTED_STORAGE_CONFIG: default: - S3Storage - s3_bucket: <bucket_name> storage_path: /registry s3_access_key: <s3_access_key> s3_region: <region> s3_secret_key: <s3_secret_key> host: <host_name>

note.p: Your DISTRIBUTED_STORAGE_CONFIG in /opt/new-quay-install must be updated before restarting your Red Hat Quay deployment.

step.cmd: Export the AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID by using the access_key credential obtained in Step 13:
Export the AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY by using the secret_key obtained in Step 13:
Create a new s3 bucket by entering the following command:
Upload all blobs to the new s3 bucket by entering the following command:

dd.p: Specifies the Red Hat Quay registry endpoint. The endpoint must be the same before backup and after restore.
dd.codeblock: upload: ../../tmp/quay-backup/blob-backup/datastorage/registry/sha256/50/505edb46ea5d32b5cbe275eb766d960842a52ee77ac225e4dc8abb12f409a30d to s3://quay/datastorage/registry/sha256/50/505edb46ea5d32b5cbe275eb766d960842a52ee77ac225e4dc8abb12f409a30d upload: ../../tmp/quay-backup/blob-backup/datastorage/registry/sha256/27/27930dc06c2ee27ac6f543ba0e93640dd21eea458eac47355e8e5989dea087d0 to s3://quay/datastorage/registry/sha256/27/27930dc06c2ee27ac6f543ba0e93640dd21eea458eac47355e8e5989dea087d0 upload: ../../tmp/quay-backup/blob-backup/datastorage/registry/sha256/8c/8c7daf5e20eee45ffe4b36761c4bb6729fb3ee60d4f588f712989939323110ec to s3://quay/datastorage/registry/sha256/8c/8c7daf5e20eee45ffe4b36761c4bb6729fb3ee60d4f588f712989939323110ec ...

step.cmd: Before restarting your Red Hat Quay deployment, update the storage settings in your config.yaml file:

info.codeblock: DISTRIBUTED_STORAGE_CONFIG: default: DISTRIBUTED_STORAGE_CONFIG: default: - S3Storage - s3_bucket: <new_bucket_name> storage_path: /registry s3_access_key: <s3_access_key> s3_secret_key: <s3_secret_key> s3_region: <region> host: <host_name>
